public_rationale: The forecast has a condition and no deadline. It says Claude Code will raise coder productivity if technical debt does not cancel the gains. Settling it needs a rigorous study of Claude Code itself that measures net productivity after technical debt. The evidence collected for this case contains no such study, so the early-resolution rule is not met. The one study cited (e1, arXiv preprint, version dated 2026-01-27) looks at coding agents in general in open-source repositories, not Claude Code alone. It found large early velocity gains only when an agent was the first AI tool in a project. Gains were small or short-lived where AI IDEs were already in use. Static-analysis warnings rose by roughly 18% and cognitive complexity by roughly 39%, and these increases persisted. This is background only. It does not show whether Claude Code raises net productivity or whether the condition holds. The forecast is still open.
limitations: The only cited study (e1) covers coding agents in general and does not isolate Claude Code.
e1 measures velocity and code-quality indicators, not net developer productivity after maintenance costs.
The evidence does not show whether the condition (technical debt not cancelling the gains) holds for Claude Code.
The claim gives no size of gain and no deadline.
